# webhooks.cc

> Webhook testing tools for developers. Capture, inspect, forward, and test webhooks with a dashboard, CLI, TypeScript SDK, and MCP server for AI agents.

## What is webhooks.cc?

webhooks.cc is a webhook inspection and testing service. Developers use it to capture incoming HTTP requests at unique URLs, inspect headers and bodies in real time, configure mock responses with conditional rules (route different responses based on method, path, headers, body, or query params), forward webhooks to localhost for local development, and write automated test assertions against captured requests.

Every endpoint on an account also receives email at its own address, so a signup flow that sends a webhook and a confirmation email can be checked in one place, and captured email can be forwarded to your server as signed JSON.

Requests are captured by a Rust receiver, written directly to Postgres via a single stored procedure, and surfaced in the dashboard through Supabase Realtime.

## Core capabilities

- Webhook capture: Send any HTTP request to https://go.webhooks.cc/w/<slug> and inspect it instantly
- Email capture: Every endpoint on an account receives email at <slug>@mailhooks.cc; each email is stored as a request with `kind: "email"` and the parsed message, and the dashboard shows its one-time codes, links, and SPF, DKIM and DMARC results
- Email forwarding: Forward every email an endpoint captures to your HTTPS URL as parsed JSON, signed with Standard Webhooks headers and retried for about a day
- Mock responses: Configure status codes, headers, and response bodies per endpoint, with conditional rules that route different responses based on method, path, headers, body content, JSON paths, or query params (first match wins)
- CLI tunneling: Forward webhooks to localhost with `whk tunnel <port>`, no port forwarding or ngrok needed
- TypeScript SDK: `@webhooks-cc/sdk` for programmatic endpoint management, test assertions, and real-time streaming; `client.emails.waitFor()` and `extractCode()` for email tests, `client.forwarding` and `verifyForwardedEmail()` for email forwarding
- Python and Go SDKs: `webhooks-cc` on PyPI and `webhooks.cc/go`, with the same waits, signed sends and signature checks, plus pytest fixtures and Go test helpers
- MCP server: the remote server at https://webhooks.cc/mcp connects coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex) and hosted agents (claude.ai, ChatGPT) with one OAuth approval in the browser; the local `@webhooks-cc/mcp` adds sends to localhost and a keyless sandbox
- Agent sandbox: AI agents capture webhooks without an account (3 endpoints for 24 hours) and connect to a human's account once; the connection is saved and shared by the MCP server, the SDKs and the CLI
- Real-time streaming: Dashboard updates via Supabase Realtime Broadcast signals, CLI and SDK via Server-Sent Events
- Request replay: Resend captured requests to any URL
- Provider detection: Built-in helpers for Stripe, GitHub, Shopify, Slack, Twilio, Paddle, and Linear webhooks

## Pricing

- Guest (no signup): 25 requests per ephemeral endpoint, deleted after 12 hours, no email capture
- Free: 50 requests per 24 hours, unlimited endpoints, 7-day retention, 20 parsed attachment pages a month, 2 layouts per endpoint, 5 AI assists every 30 days, every Pro feature including email capture, Google Sheets and chat destinations and full CLI/SDK/MCP access
- Pro ($8/month): 100,000 requests per 30 days, 31-day retention, 100 parsed attachment pages a month, 20 AI assists every 30 days, extra requests in blocks of 25,000
- Business ($29/month or $290/year): 250,000 requests a month, 90-day retention, 2,000 parsed attachment pages a month (then page blocks or page overage), up to 50 layouts per endpoint, 500 AI assists every 30 days, one custom inbound domain (extra ones $3/month), file drops to SFTP, FTP/FTPS or S3, extra requests as on Pro; on annual billing requests and pages still reset every month
- Teams ($12/seat/month): a separate per-team subscription; each seat adds 100,000 requests per 30 days to a pooled team quota, and requests on endpoints shared with the team are kept 31 days. The Team Business add-on ($49/month) adds 150,000 requests, 2,000 pooled parsed pages a month, up to 50 layouts per shared endpoint, 500 AI assists, one custom inbound domain, file drops and 90-day retention
- Emails count against the same quota as webhooks: one request per email per endpoint

## For AI agents: start here

Take the first option that fits.

1. Your client can add a remote MCP server, and a human is around: use the remote server. This is the default for coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex) as much as for hosted ones (claude.ai, ChatGPT). The one exception is a task that sends to a handler on this machine (`send_to`, `replay_request`, `targetUrl`), which the remote server cannot reach: take option 2 for that, or send to a capture URL and forward it with `whk tunnel <port>`. The server is https://webhooks.cc/mcp (streamable HTTP, OAuth). Your human signs in, or signs up, and clicks Connect once in the browser: no code to type, nothing that expires after 24 hours, and their account's tools (mock responses, forwarding, signature checks, email). Suggest it with the line for your client:
   - Claude Code: `claude mcp add -s user --transport http webhooks-cc https://webhooks.cc/mcp`, then `/mcp` in Claude Code to sign in
   - Codex: `codex mcp add webhooks-cc --url https://webhooks.cc/mcp` (it opens the browser to sign in; if it does not, `codex mcp login webhooks-cc`)
   - Cursor, in `.cursor/mcp.json`: `{ "mcpServers": { "webhooks-cc": { "url": "https://webhooks.cc/mcp" } } }`
   - VS Code, in `.vscode/mcp.json`: `{ "servers": { "webhooks-cc": { "type": "http", "url": "https://webhooks.cc/mcp" } } }`
   - claude.ai and Claude Desktop: in Settings, Connectors, add a custom connector with the URL https://webhooks.cc/mcp. ChatGPT: add it as a custom connector (in developer mode)
   - Any other client: add https://webhooks.cc/mcp as a remote (streamable HTTP) server

   Then stop and hand over. Tools from a newly added server appear only after your client reconnects or restarts, so wait for your human there; do not start a sandbox claim as well. Setup for each client: https://webhooks.cc/docs/mcp#remote-server. A client that can send headers may use an API key instead: `Authorization: Bearer whcc_...`.

Options 2 to 5 are the fallback, and they start in the sandbox. It needs nothing from your human: it is free, anonymous, isolated from every account, and deleted after 24 hours. It lacks more than 3 endpoints, mock responses, forwarding, signature checks and email. Pick it when nobody wants an account, for throwaway captures, in CI, or with no human present. Your human can still keep what you made there through the claim; the remote server does not move sandbox endpoints into the account.

2. The local MCP server, for clients that run local (stdio) servers: `claude mcp add webhooks-cc -- npx -y @webhooks-cc/mcp`, or `npx -y @webhooks-cc/mcp setup cursor` (or `vscode`, `codex`, `windsurf`, `claude-desktop`). No key needed: your first `create_endpoint` registers a sandbox; `connect_account` then `wait_for_connection` moves everything into your human's account. Connected to an account (an API key or a claim), the local server is also the one you need to send to localhost (`send_to`, `replay_request`, `targetUrl`) and for its prompts and resources, which the remote server lacks.
3. Claude Code with plugins: `/plugin install webhooks-cc --marketplace kroqdotdev/webhooks-cc` (the local MCP server plus the webhook-testing skill).
4. You can run code. Each of these registers, solves the proof of work and reuses the sandbox on the next run:
   - Python: `pip install webhooks-cc`, then `WebhooksCC.sandbox()`
   - Node: `npm i @webhooks-cc/sdk`, then `WebhooksCC.sandbox()`
   - Go: `go get webhooks.cc/go`, then `webhookscc.NewSandbox(ctx)`
   - Shell: `whk sandbox create --json` (install with `curl -fsSL https://webhooks.cc/install.sh | sh` or `brew install kroqdotdev/tap/whk`; without root, `curl -fsSL https://webhooks.cc/install.sh | WHK_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin" sh`)
5. Only HTTP: follow the steps in https://webhooks.cc/auth.md.

For the claim email, use the address your human signs in to webhooks.cc with (their GitHub or Google primary email if they sign in that way). Your human has an API key? Set `WHK_API_KEY` and skip all of this.

## Agent credential file

Options 2 to 4 keep the sandbox and the human's connection in one file and reuse it, so the human approves an agent once:

~/.config/whk/agent.json                       # Linux, or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/whk/agent.json
~/Library/Application Support/whk/agent.json   # macOS
%APPDATA%\whk\agent.json                       # Windows

`WHK_AGENT_FILE` overrides the path. The file is JSON (version 1) with a `claimed` slot (a connection to a human's account, 90 days) and a `sandbox` slot (24 hours) under each app URL, written atomically with mode 0600. The claim token is never written. An explicit API key wins over the file; then a live `claimed` slot; then the sandbox. Read it before registering again: `WebhooksCC.connected()` in the SDKs does. Format: https://webhooks.cc/docs/agents#the-agent-credential-file

## API key format

All API keys use the prefix `whcc_`. Keys are generated via the CLI with `whk auth login` or from the account page after signing in. Access tokens that agents get through auth.md or OAuth use the same prefix and the same `Authorization: Bearer` header. See https://webhooks.cc/docs for setup instructions.

## Webhook endpoint URL format

https://go.webhooks.cc/w/<slug>
https://go.webhooks.cc/w/<slug>/optional/path

Any HTTP method, content type, and body up to 1 MB is accepted.

## Email address format

<slug>@mailhooks.cc
<slug>+<tag>@mailhooks.cc

Endpoints on an account receive email; guest endpoints do not. Messages up to 10 MB are accepted. The tag after the plus sign lands on the same endpoint and is kept on the captured email. mailhooks.cc only receives mail and never sends any.

## CLI commands

whk                  # Interactive TUI
whk auth login       # Authenticate via browser
whk auth status      # Show login status
whk auth logout      # Clear stored token
whk tunnel <port>    # Forward webhooks to localhost
whk listen <slug>    # Stream requests to terminal
whk create [name]    # Create endpoint
whk list             # List endpoints
whk delete <slug>    # Delete endpoint
whk replay <id>      # Replay captured request
whk update           # Self-update from GitHub releases

whk sandbox create --json                # Capture without an account (AI agents)
whk sandbox wait <slug> --json           # Wait for a request to arrive
whk sandbox list|get|delete|requests|request|status|forget
whk sandbox connect --email <address>    # Prints a link and a code, waits for the human

## SDK quick start

```typescript
import { WebhooksCC, matchBodyPath } from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";

const client = new WebhooksCC({ apiKey: process.env.WHK_API_KEY });

// Create an endpoint with conditional response rules
const endpoint = await client.endpoints.create({
  name: "test",
  responseRules: [
    {
      name: "Stripe invoices",
      conditions: [
        { field: "header", op: "exists", name: "stripe-signature" },
        { field: "body_path", op: "eq", path: "type", value: "invoice.paid" },
      ],
      response: { status: 200, body: '{"received": true}', headers: {} },
    },
  ],
  mockResponse: { status: 200, body: "ok", headers: {} }, // default fallback
});
console.log(endpoint.url); // https://go.webhooks.cc/w/<slug>

// Wait for a webhook to arrive
const request = await client.requests.waitFor(endpoint.slug, {
  timeout: "30s",
  match: matchBodyPath("event", "payment.success"),
});

// Stream requests in real time
for await (const req of client.requests.subscribe(endpoint.slug)) {
  console.log(req.method, req.path);
}

// Clean up
await client.endpoints.delete(endpoint.slug);
```

## MCP server setup

The remote server at https://webhooks.cc/mcp is the recommended way in: no key and nothing to install, one approval in the browser. It has the same tools as the local server except `send_to` and `replay_request` (a hosted server cannot reach your machine), and no prompts or resources.

```bash
# Claude Code, remote MCP server (then /mcp in Claude Code to sign in)
claude mcp add -s user --transport http webhooks-cc https://webhooks.cc/mcp

# Codex, remote MCP server (opens the browser to sign in)
codex mcp add webhooks-cc --url https://webhooks.cc/mcp
```

Cursor, in `.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "webhooks-cc": { "url": "https://webhooks.cc/mcp" } } }
```

VS Code, in `.vscode/mcp.json`:

```json
{ "servers": { "webhooks-cc": { "type": "http", "url": "https://webhooks.cc/mcp" } } }
```

In claude.ai and Claude Desktop, add https://webhooks.cc/mcp as a custom connector under Settings, Connectors; in ChatGPT, as a custom connector in developer mode.

The agent skill tells Cursor, Codex, Copilot and other agents when to use these tools, with either server: `npx skills add kroqdotdev/webhooks-cc`.

The local server, `@webhooks-cc/mcp`, is for sending to localhost, its prompts and resources, the keyless sandbox, and CI:

```bash
# Claude Code: plugin with the local MCP server and the webhook testing skill
/plugin install webhooks-cc --marketplace kroqdotdev/webhooks-cc

# Claude Code, local MCP server only
claude mcp add webhooks-cc -- npx -y @webhooks-cc/mcp

# Cursor / VS Code / Windsurf (also codex and claude-desktop)
npx @webhooks-cc/mcp setup cursor
npx @webhooks-cc/mcp setup vscode
npx @webhooks-cc/mcp setup windsurf
```

`WHK_API_KEY` is optional. Without it the local server starts with the full tools when the human connected the agent before (saved in the agent credential file), and otherwise in the keyless sandbox, where `connect_account` and `wait_for_connection` connect an account. To start with your account's tools, set `WHK_API_KEY` or pass `--api-key whcc_...` to `setup`.
